stemText: If A and B are square matrices of the same order such that AB = A + B, then which of the following is always true?

solution.explanationText: From AB = A + B, rearrange terms: AB - A - B = O => AB - A - B + I = I => (A - I)(B - I) = I. Since (A - I) and (B - I) are inverses of each other, they commute: (B - I)(A - I) = I => BA - B - A + I = I => BA = A + B. Because both AB and BA equal A + B, we obtain AB = BA.
